Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *derḱ-der.
Proto-Hellenic *dérkomai
Ancient Greek δέρκομαι (dérkomai)
Ancient Greek δρᾰ́κων ~ δρᾰ́κοντος (drắkōn ~ drắkontos)
Proto-Indo-European *-yóm
Proto-Hellenic
Ancient Greek -ῐον (-ĭon)
Ancient Greek δρακόντιον (drakóntion)der.
Arabic طرخون
From Ancient Greek δρακόντιον (drakóntion, “edder-wort, Dracunculus vulgaris”, a plant with similar leaves, confused in pharmacopoeiae as both plants were not everywhere available), from δράκων (drákōn, “dragon, serpent”) relating to the shape of its leaves.
